q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the capital outlay on other agricultural programmes, not covered by the specific agricultural capital heads, is accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 4408 - Capital Outlay on Food Storage and Warehousing
options.B: 4415 - Capital Outlay on Agricultural Research and Education
options.C: 4435 - Capital Outlay on Other Agricultural Programmes
options.D: 4425 - Capital Outlay on Co-operation

e: Capital outlay on other agricultural programmes not covered by specific heads is classified under Major Head 4435 - Capital Outlay on Other Agricultural Programmes.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the loans given for ports and light houses are accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 7051 - Loans for Ports and Light Houses
options.B: 7052 - Loans for Shipping
options.C: 7053 - Loans for Civil Aviation
options.D: 7055 - Loans for Road Transport

e: Loans for ports and light houses are classified under Major Head 7051 - Loans for Ports and Light Houses in the loans and advances section.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the loans given for shipping are accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 7051 - Loans for Ports and Light Houses
options.B: 7053 - Loans for Civil Aviation
options.C: 7056 - Loans for Inland Water Transport
options.D: 7052 - Loans for Shipping

e: Loans for shipping are classified under Major Head 7052 - Loans for Shipping, as per the List of Major and Minor Heads of Account.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the loans given for road transport are accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 7051 - Loans for Ports and Light Houses
options.B: 7055 - Loans for Road Transport
options.C: 7052 - Loans for Shipping
options.D: 7056 - Loans for Inland Water Transport

e: Loans for road transport are classified under Major Head 7055 - Loans for Road Transport in the Government system of classification.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the loans given for inland water transport are accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 7052 - Loans for Shipping
options.B: 7053 - Loans for Civil Aviation
options.C: 7056 - Loans for Inland Water Transport
options.D: 7055 - Loans for Road Transport

e: Loans for inland water transport are classified under Major Head 7056 - Loans for Inland Water Transport, as per the prescribed list of heads.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the loans given for medical and public health are accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 6210 - Loans for Medical and Public Health
options.B: 6202 - Loans for Education, Sports, Art and Culture
options.C: 6215 - Loans for Water Supply and Sanitation
options.D: 6216 - Loans for Housing

e: Loans for medical and public health are classified under Major Head 6210 - Loans for Medical and Public Health in the social services loans section.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the loans given for the welfare of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes and Minorities are accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 6217 - Loans for Urban Development
options.B: 6220 - Loans for Information and Publicity
options.C: 6235 - Loans for Social Security and Welfare
options.D: 6225 - Loans for Welfare of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes and Minorities

e: Loans for welfare of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes and Minorities are classified under Major Head 6225, the specific head for that purpose.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes cost audit from financial audit?

options.A: Cost audit is conducted by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, while financial audit is conducted by the organisation's own staff
options.B: Cost audit is concerned only with the arithmetical accuracy of the cash book, while financial audit examines the cost of production
options.C: Cost audit examines the correctness of the cost accounts and the cost of production of an undertaking, while financial audit examines whether the financial statements present the financial position in accordance with the applicable framework
options.D: There is no difference between cost audit and financial audit

e: Cost audit verifies cost accounts and the cost of production, while financial audit examines whether financial statements fairly present the position under the applicable framework.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes inherent risk from control risk in audit?

options.A: Inherent risk is the risk that the auditor expresses a wrong opinion, while control risk is the risk of fraud by the management
options.B: Inherent risk is the susceptibility of an assertion to a material misstatement before considering any related controls, while control risk is the risk that a material misstatement is not prevented, or detected and corrected, by the entity's internal control
options.C: Inherent risk arises from weaknesses in internal control, while control risk arises from the nature of the business itself
options.D: Inherent risk and control risk are two names for the same risk

e: Inherent risk is susceptibility to material misstatement before controls, assuming no related controls, while control risk is the risk that internal control fails to prevent or detect it.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the sufficiency of audit evidence from its appropriateness?

options.A: Sufficiency is the measure of the quantity of audit evidence, while appropriateness is the measure of its quality, that is, its relevance and reliability
options.B: Sufficiency is the measure of the quality of audit evidence, while appropriateness is the measure of its quantity
options.C: Sufficiency relates to evidence obtained from outside the entity, while appropriateness relates to evidence obtained from within the entity
options.D: Sufficiency and appropriateness are two names for the same quality of audit evidence

e: Sufficiency is the quantity of audit evidence obtained, while appropriateness is its quality, judged by relevance and reliability for supporting audit conclusions.

q: In audit sampling, 'attribute sampling' is primarily used to:

options.A: Estimate the total monetary value of errors in a population
options.B: Verify the closing balances of assets and liabilities
options.C: Value the stock-in-trade of the audited unit
options.D: Test the rate of deviation from a prescribed control procedure in the population

e: Attribute sampling is used in tests of controls to estimate the rate of deviation from a prescribed control procedure in the population.

q: An 'interim audit' is best described as an audit which is:

options.A: Conducted only after the close of the financial year, on the final accounts
options.B: Conducted by the staff of the audited office itself
options.C: Conducted during the course of the accounting period, before its close, so that the final audit is facilitated
options.D: Conducted only of the cash balances of an office

e: Interim audit is carried out during the accounting period, before its close, covering transactions up to that date so that the final audit can be completed more quickly.

q: In audit sampling, the 'projected misstatement' in a population is:

options.A: The misstatement which the auditor decides to tolerate in the population
options.B: The misstatement found in the sample, extrapolated to the population as a whole on the basis of the sampling results
options.C: The maximum misstatement that can remain undetected in the accounts
options.D: The misstatement projected by the management in its estimates

e: Projected misstatement is the misstatement found in the sample extrapolated to the whole population on the basis of the sampling results.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'efficiency' from 'effectiveness' in performance audit?

options.A: Efficiency relates the outputs produced to the inputs used, while effectiveness relates the results achieved to the objectives intended to be achieved
options.B: Efficiency and effectiveness are two names for the same concept
options.C: Efficiency is concerned only with financial results, while effectiveness is concerned only with physical targets
options.D: Efficiency is concerned with the achievement of objectives, while effectiveness is concerned with the cost of inputs

e: Efficiency relates outputs to inputs used, while effectiveness relates results actually achieved to the objectives intended to be achieved.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a 'fraud' from an 'error' in the accounts?

options.A: A fraud results in a large monetary loss, while an error results only in a small loss
options.B: A fraud is detected by audit, while an error is detected only by internal check
options.C: A fraud relates to cash transactions, while an error relates only to stores transactions
options.D: A fraud is an intentional act resulting in a misstatement, while an error is an unintentional mistake in the accounts

e: The distinguishing feature is intent: fraud is an intentional act causing misstatement, while error is an unintentional mistake in the accounts.

q: An 'Emphasis of Matter' paragraph in an auditor's report serves to:

options.A: Qualify the opinion expressed by the auditor on the financial statements
options.B: Express an adverse opinion on the financial statements
options.C: Draw attention to a matter already presented or disclosed in the financial statements, which is of such importance that it is fundamental to the users' understanding of the statements, without qualifying the opinion
options.D: Record the auditor's inability to obtain sufficient audit evidence

e: An Emphasis of Matter paragraph draws attention to a matter properly disclosed in the statements that is fundamental to users' understanding, without qualifying the audit opinion.

q: In the commercial accounts of Indian Railways, 'Demands Payable' represents:

options.A: The amounts demanded by the staff of the Railway as arrears of pay
options.B: The liabilities incurred but not discharged at the close of the year, taken into account so that the working expenses of the year are complete in the commercial accounts
options.C: The grants demanded by the Railway from Parliament for the next year
options.D: The amounts recoverable by the Railway from other Railways

e: Demands Payable are liabilities incurred but not discharged at year-end, brought into Railway commercial accounts so that working expenses of the year are complete.

q: In the commercial accounts of Indian Railways, 'Demands Recoverable' represents:

options.A: The amounts due to the Railway, for services rendered or supplies made, which have been taken to account in the commercial accounts but have not yet been actually recovered
options.B: The demands made by the Railway on the staff for recovery of overpayments
options.C: The budget demands recoverable from the Ministry of Finance
options.D: The loans advanced by the Railway to its employees

e: Demands Recoverable are amounts due to Railways for services or supplies, taken into commercial accounts as earnings although not yet actually recovered in cash.

q: Expenditure which is unnecessary and from which no useful result can be expected is termed by Audit as:

options.A: Infructuous expenditure
options.B: Irregular expenditure
options.C: Unsanctioned expenditure
options.D: Nugatory expenditure

e: Nugatory expenditure is expenditure that is unnecessary and from which no useful result can be expected, as distinct from infructuous expenditure actually incurred in vain.

q: In British budgetary terminology, 'virement' corresponds to the device known in Indian Government accounts as:

options.A: A Vote on Account
options.B: A Supplementary Grant
options.C: Re-appropriation of funds from one head of account to another within a grant
options.D: Surrender of savings in a grant

e: Virement in British terminology is transfer of provision from one head to another within a grant, which in Indian Government accounts is called re-appropriation.

q: A 'poll tax' in public finance is a tax which is:

options.A: Levied at a fixed amount on every adult person, irrespective of his income or property
options.B: Levied only on the occasion of a general election
options.C: Levied on goods at the point of their entry into a local area
options.D: Levied as a percentage of the profits of a company

e: A poll tax is a tax levied at a fixed amount on every adult person, irrespective of income, property or ability to pay.

q: The 'deadweight loss' of a tax refers to:

options.A: The loss of revenue suffered by the Government on account of tax evasion
options.B: The loss of economic welfare or efficiency caused by the tax, over and above the revenue raised by it
options.C: The cost incurred by the Government in collecting the tax
options.D: The loss caused to the taxpayer by the shifting of the tax

e: Deadweight loss is the loss of economic welfare caused by a tax over and above the revenue it raises, arising from distortion of production and consumption decisions.

q: The expression 'inflation tax' refers to:

options.A: A tax levied by the Government expressly to check inflation
options.B: An additional tax imposed on goods whose prices have risen
options.C: The tax collected by the Government on the profits made during inflation
options.D: The gain accruing to the Government from inflation, through the erosion of the real value of the money held by the public and of the Government's own monetary liabilities

e: Inflation tax is the gain to Government from inflation through erosion of the real value of money held by the public and of Government's own monetary liabilities.

q: A Government is said to have fallen into a 'debt trap' when:

options.A: Its total public debt exceeds the value of its assets
options.B: It raises a loan from an external agency for the first time
options.C: It is obliged to borrow increasingly merely to meet the interest payments and repayment obligations on its existing debt
options.D: Its revenue receipts fall short of its revenue expenditure in a year

e: A debt trap arises when Government must borrow increasingly merely to pay interest and repay existing debt, so debt grows without corresponding productive use.

q: The 'Ramsey rule' of optimal taxation, based on the inverse elasticity rule, suggests that, to minimise the excess burden of taxation:

options.A: Commodities whose demand is relatively inelastic should be taxed at relatively higher rates than commodities whose demand is elastic
options.B: All commodities should be taxed at one uniform rate
options.C: Commodities whose demand is elastic should be taxed at the highest rates
options.D: Only luxury goods should be taxed

e: The Ramsey inverse elasticity rule requires higher tax rates on goods with inelastic demand and lower rates on elastic goods, to minimise excess burden for a given revenue.

q: 'Fiscal illusion' in public finance refers to the situation in which:

options.A: The Government presents its deficit as smaller than it actually is
options.B: Taxpayers systematically underestimate the burden of taxation on them, particularly where the taxes are indirect or are collected in small amounts
options.C: The taxpayers are fully aware of the burden of every tax they pay
options.D: Inflation creates an illusion of rising money incomes while real incomes also rise equally

e: Fiscal illusion occurs when taxpayers underestimate their tax burden, especially where taxes are indirect, hidden in prices or collected in small amounts.

q: 'Vertical imbalance' in the finances of a federation refers to:

options.A: The imbalance between the finances of the richer States and the poorer States
options.B: The imbalance between the tax revenue and the non-tax revenue of the Central Government
options.C: The imbalance between the revenue receipts and the capital receipts of a State
options.D: The mismatch between the revenue-raising powers assigned to a level of Government and the expenditure responsibilities assigned to it

e: Vertical imbalance is the mismatch between revenue-raising powers assigned to a level of Government in a federation and the expenditure responsibilities assigned to it.

q: A 'matching grant' given by the Central Government to a State Government is a grant which is:

options.A: Equal in amount to the grant given to every other State
options.B: Given to match the growth of the State's own tax revenue
options.C: Conditional upon the State Government contributing a prescribed share of the cost of the scheme or purpose for which the grant is given
options.D: Given only for meeting natural calamities

e: A matching grant is conditional on the State contributing a prescribed share of the cost of the scheme or purpose for which the Central grant is given.

q: The maximum amount of tax on professions, trades, callings and employments which a State Legislature may levy on a person in a year, as laid down in Article 276 of the Constitution, is:
e: Article 276 caps the tax on professions, trades, callings and employments levied by a State at Rs 2,500 per person per year.

q: In a House of Parliament, the presiding officer, in his capacity as such:

options.A: Does not ordinarily vote in the first instance, but exercises a casting vote in the case of an equality of votes
options.B: Votes in the first instance like every other member, and has no casting vote
options.C: Exercises two votes on every question before the House
options.D: Cannot vote even when the votes are equally divided

e: Under Article 100, the presiding officer does not vote in the first instance but exercises a casting vote when votes on a question are equally divided.

q: Under Article 100 of the Constitution, the quorum required to constitute a meeting of a House of Parliament is:

options.A: One-half of the total number of members of the House
options.B: One-third of the total number of members of the House
options.C: One-fifth of the total number of members of the House
options.D: One-tenth of the total number of members of the House

e: Article 100 fixes the quorum for a meeting of either House of Parliament at one-tenth of the total number of members of the House.

q: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India is popularly described as the:

options.A: Watchdog of the Estimates Committee
options.B: Financial adviser of Parliament
options.C: Guardian of the public purse
options.D: Chief accounting authority of the Union

e: The CAG, as independent auditor of Government accounts on behalf of Parliament and the Legislatures, is popularly called the guardian of the public purse.

q: Dr B. R. Ambedkar described the office which he considered to be probably the most important office under the Constitution of India as that of:

options.A: The Attorney General of India
options.B: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.C: The Chief Election Commissioner
options.D: The Chairman of the Finance Commission

e: Dr B. R. Ambedkar described the Comptroller and Auditor General as probably the most important officer under the Constitution of India.

q: 'Management audit' is primarily concerned with:

options.A: Appraising the policies, procedures and performance of the management of an organisation as a whole, with a view to improving its efficiency and effectiveness
options.B: Verifying the cash balance held by the cashier of an office
options.C: Auditing the accounts of a Government company on behalf of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: Inspecting the offices subordinate to a controlling authority

e: Management audit appraises policies, procedures and performance of management as a whole, with a view to improving efficiency and effectiveness of the organisation.

q: Government securities are popularly described as 'gilt-edged' securities because:

options.A: They are printed on paper with gilt edges
options.B: They are issued only against gold reserves
options.C: They can be purchased only by banks and financial institutions
options.D: They are regarded as exceptionally safe investments, being obligations of the Government

e: Government securities are called gilt-edged because they are obligations of Government and are therefore regarded as exceptionally safe investments.

q: In the Demands for Grants presented to Parliament, the provisions relating to 'charged' expenditure are distinguished from the voted provisions by being printed in:

options.A: Bold type
options.B: Capital letters
options.C: Italics
options.D: A separate volume

e: In the Demands for Grants, charged expenditure is distinguished from voted expenditure by being printed in italics, while voted provisions are in ordinary type.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The balances of the Railway Funds, such as the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Development Fund, are held in the Public Account of India.
2. Appropriations to the Railway Funds are made out of the revenues of the Railways.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Railway fund balances such as Depreciation Reserve Fund and Development Fund are held in the Public Account, and appropriations to them are made from railway revenues. Both statements are correct.

q: In the List of Major and Minor Heads of Account, the Major Heads in the 6000 and 7000 series broadly relate to:

options.A: Public debt, loans and advances
options.B: Revenue receipts of the Government
options.C: Revenue expenditure of the Government
options.D: Deposits and advances in the Public Account

e: In the List of Major and Minor Heads, the 6000 series covers public debt and the 7000 series covers loans and advances made by Government.

q: Internal audit in an organisation differs from the statutory audit of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India in that the scope and programme of internal audit are determined by:

options.A: Parliament
options.B: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.C: The Finance Commission
options.D: The management of the organisation itself

e: Internal audit is an appraisal activity within the organisation, so its scope and programme are determined by the management itself, unlike statutory audit by the CAG.

q: The Balance Sheet forming part of the commercial accounts of Indian Railways shows, on its liabilities side, among other items:

options.A: Only the stores held in stock by the Railway
options.B: Only the loans raised by the Railway from the market during the year
options.C: The capital-at-charge of the Railway and the balances standing to the credit of its various funds
options.D: The grants voted by Parliament for the Railway during the year

e: The Railway Balance Sheet shows on the liabilities side the capital-at-charge and the balances at credit of the various railway funds, against the assets of the undertaking.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A company in which not less than 51 per cent of the paid-up share capital is held by the Government is a 'Government company' for the purposes of audit by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
2. A company which is a subsidiary of a Government company is also treated as a Government company.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Under the Companies Act definition used for CAG audit, a Government company has at least 51 per cent Government shareholding, and a subsidiary of such a company is also a Government company. Both are correct.

q: During audit of a works expenditure, the audit party confines itself to seeing that the sanction behind the expenditure was issued by an authority competent to issue it and that the sanction conforms to the applicable rules. This scrutiny is an instance of:

options.A: Audit against sanctions
options.B: Audit against provision of funds
options.C: Performance audit
options.D: Propriety audit

e: Checking that expenditure rests on a sanction of the competent authority issued in conformity with rules is audit against sanctions, distinct from audit against provision of funds.

q: A test audit of a small office brings out only minor irregularities which do not call for a detailed Inspection Report. Audit brings such irregularities to the notice of the executive through:

options.A: A Draft Para
options.B: An Audit Para
options.C: The Appropriation Accounts
options.D: A Test Audit Note

e: Minor irregularities noticed in test audit that do not warrant an Inspection Report are communicated to the executive through a Test Audit Note.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'central audit' from 'local audit' in the organisation of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India?

options.A: Central audit is conducted by the staff of the Central Government, while local audit is conducted by the staff of the State Government
options.B: Central audit is conducted at the headquarters office of the audit organisation, to which the vouchers and accounts of the units concerned are sent, while local audit is conducted at the premises of the unit
options.C: Central audit covers only the accounts of the Railway Board, while local audit covers the accounts of the zonal Railways
options.D: Central audit is limited to one selected month, while local audit covers the whole year

e: Central audit is done at the audit headquarters on vouchers and accounts sent there, while local audit is done on the premises of the audited unit itself.

q: On a zonal Railway, proposals with financial implications are examined in the office of the officer who functions as the principal financial adviser to the General Manager. That officer is the:

options.A: Financial Adviser and Chief Accounts Officer
options.B: Principal Director of Audit
options.C: Financial Commissioner (Railways)
options.D: Chief Vigilance Officer

e: On a zonal Railway the Financial Adviser and Chief Accounts Officer is the principal financial adviser to the General Manager and examines proposals with financial implications.

q: The fund created for clearing the backlog of safety-related renewal works of track, bridges, signalling and rolling stock was set up on the recommendations of the:

options.A: Acworth Committee
options.B: Railway Safety Review Committee (Khanna Committee)
options.C: Bibek Debroy Committee
options.D: Railway Convention Committee of 1949

e: The Special Railway Safety Fund for clearing backlog of safety renewals was set up following the recommendations of the Railway Safety Review Committee, the Khanna Committee.

q: Which of the following committees is associated with the recommendation that led to the merger of the Railway Budget with the General Budget?

options.A: The Acworth Committee
options.B: The Khanna Committee
options.C: The Kunzru Committee
options.D: The Bibek Debroy Committee

e: The merger of the Railway Budget with the General Budget followed the recommendation of the Bibek Debroy Committee on restructuring of Railways.

q: In the capital expenditure plan of Indian Railways, the support provided from the Union Budget is referred to as:

options.A: Extra Budgetary Resources
options.B: Internal resources of Railways
options.C: Gross Budgetary Support
options.D: Market borrowings through IRFC

e: Support provided to Railways from the Union Budget for its capital expenditure plan is termed Gross Budgetary Support, distinct from internal and extra-budgetary resources.

q: A person assumes charge as the Comptroller and Auditor General of India on appointment made by the President under Article 148 of the Constitution. The instrument of his appointment is:

options.A: A resolution of both Houses of Parliament
options.B: An order of the Public Accounts Committee
options.C: A warrant under the hand and seal of the President
options.D: A notification issued by the Ministry of Finance

e: Under Article 148, the CAG is appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal, securing the independence of the office.

q: A Demand for Grant is sought to be presented to the Lok Sabha without the recommendation of the President. Under Article 113 of the Constitution, the correct position is that:

options.A: The Demand can be presented with the approval of the Estimates Committee
options.B: The Demand can be presented with the concurrence of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.C: The Demand can be presented after the general discussion on the Budget
options.D: No Demand for a grant shall be made except on the recommendation of the President

e: Article 113(3) expressly provides that no Demand for a grant shall be made except on the recommendation of the President.

q: A department proposes to withdraw moneys out of the Consolidated Fund of India on the strength of the Budget Estimates alone, without waiting for an Appropriation Act. Article 266(3) of the Constitution bars this because no moneys out of the Consolidated Fund of India shall be appropriated except:

options.A: In accordance with law, that is, under the authority of an Appropriation Act passed by Parliament
options.B: With the concurrence of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.C: With the approval of the Estimates Committee
options.D: Under an order of the Finance Minister

e: Article 266(3) bars withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund except in accordance with law, so Budget Estimates alone do not suffice; an Appropriation Act is required.

q: The provision of the Comptroller and Auditor General's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971 under which the audit of the accounts of Government companies is dealt with is:

options.A: Section 16
options.B: Section 19
options.C: Section 17
options.D: Section 13

e: Section 19 of the CAG's DPC Act, 1971 deals with audit of accounts of Government companies, supplementing the audit provisions of company law.

q: The salary payable to the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is fixed by the Constitution at par with the salary of:

options.A: The Chief Justice of India
options.B: A Cabinet Minister
options.C: A Judge of the Supreme Court
options.D: The Governor of the Reserve Bank of India

e: The salary of the CAG is fixed at par with that of a Judge of the Supreme Court, as provided in the CAG's DPC Act, 1971 to protect his independence.

q: The members of the Public Accounts Committee are chosen by each House of Parliament from amongst its members according to the principle of:

options.A: Nomination by the President
options.B: Simple majority in a joint sitting
options.C: Nomination by the Speaker and the Chairman jointly
options.D: Proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote

e: Members of the Public Accounts Committee are elected by each House from amongst its members by proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.

q: Among the functions of the Estimates Committee is to suggest:

options.A: The form in which the estimates shall be presented to Parliament
options.B: The rate of dividend payable by Railways to General Finances
options.C: The fare and freight structure of Railways
options.D: The composition of the Railway Board

e: A stated function of the Estimates Committee is to suggest the form in which the estimates shall be presented to Parliament, besides suggesting economies and improvements.

q: The Committee on Public Undertakings of Parliament is constituted with:

options.A: 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha
options.B: 22 members — 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha
options.C: 15 members, all from the Rajya Sabha
options.D: 45 members drawn from both Houses

e: The Committee on Public Undertakings has 22 members, 15 elected by Lok Sabha and 7 by Rajya Sabha, to examine public undertakings including CAG reports on them.

q: Which of the following correctly brings out the position of the Public Accounts Committee in relation to questions of policy?

options.A: It frames the policy underlying each Demand for Grant
options.B: It examines the estimates and suggests the policy to be followed
options.C: It can disallow an item of expenditure on policy grounds
options.D: It examines the accounts after the expenditure is incurred and does not go into questions of policy

e: The Public Accounts Committee examines accounts after expenditure is incurred and keeps to appropriation and audit; it does not go into questions of policy underlying the grants.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'internal control' from 'internal check'?

options.A: Internal control is the whole system of controls, financial and otherwise, established by the management, of which internal check and internal audit are parts
options.B: Internal control is the check exercised by the audit office over the accounts of a unit
options.C: Internal control is confined to the verification of the cash balance
options.D: Internal control is one part of internal check, confined to cash transactions

e: Internal control is the whole system of financial and other controls established by management, and internal check and internal audit are parts of that wider system.

q: The gross traffic earnings of a railway, for the purpose of its commercial accounts, comprise:

options.A: Passenger coaching earnings only
options.B: Goods earnings and sundry other earnings only
options.C: Passenger coaching earnings, other coaching earnings, goods earnings and sundry other earnings
options.D: Passenger coaching earnings and goods earnings only

e: Gross traffic earnings comprise passenger coaching earnings, other coaching earnings, goods earnings and sundry other earnings of the Railway.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the audit of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India from the 'pre-check' exercised by the Accounts office?

options.A: The audit of the Comptroller and Auditor General is a pre-audit of every bill before payment, while pre-check is exercised after payment
options.B: The audit of the Comptroller and Auditor General is essentially a post-audit carried out after the transactions have taken place, while pre-check is exercised by the Accounts office before payment is made
options.C: Both are exercised before payment is made
options.D: Both are exercised only at the close of the financial year

e: CAG audit is essentially post-audit after transactions have occurred, while pre-check is exercised by the Accounts office on bills before payment is made.

q: Under the system of 'associated finance' followed on Railways, a proposal of the executive involving financial implications can be sanctioned only after:

options.A: The approval of the Railway Convention Committee
options.B: The vetting of the resident audit office
options.C: The approval of the Ministry of Finance in every case
options.D: The concurrence of the associated finance, that is, the organisation of the Financial Adviser and Chief Accounts Officer

e: Under associated finance on Railways, a proposal with financial implications requires concurrence of the associated finance, i.e. the FA and CAO organisation, before sanction.

q: The Departmentally Related Standing Committee on Railways, which examines the Demands for Grants of the Ministry of Railways, consists of:

options.A: 31 members — 21 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha
options.B: 22 members — 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha
options.C: 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha
options.D: 45 members drawn from both Houses

e: The Departmentally Related Standing Committee on Railways has 31 members, 21 from Lok Sabha and 10 from Rajya Sabha, and examines Demands for Grants of the Ministry.

q: An officer administering funds of a local body opens a Personal Deposit account in the Government accounts for those moneys. Such Personal Deposit accounts are maintained as part of:

options.A: The Consolidated Fund of India
options.B: The Contingency Fund of India
options.C: The Public Account of India
options.D: The Railway Development Fund

e: Personal Deposit accounts for moneys of local bodies and others administered by Government officers are maintained as part of the Public Account of India.

q: A fund on Indian Railways was created primarily to provide a cushion for meeting the debt-service (lease) obligations arising out of market borrowings raised for railway projects. The fund is the:

options.A: Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.B: Development Fund
options.C: Pension Fund
options.D: Debt Service Fund

e: The Debt Service Fund was created on Railways to provide a cushion for meeting debt-service and lease obligations arising from market borrowings for railway projects.

q: Under the financial convention in force before the merger of the Railway Budget, the loss arising on the working of strategic lines on Indian Railways was borne by:

options.A: The Railways themselves, out of their surplus
options.B: General Finances (General Revenues)
options.C: The Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.D: The State Governments through whose territory the lines passed

e: Before merger of the Railway Budget, under the financial convention the loss on working of strategic lines was borne by General Finances, not by Railways.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes Volume I from Volume II of the Indian Railway Accounts Code?

options.A: Volume I deals with the general principles of railway accounting, the books of account and the compilation of accounts other than traffic accounts, while Volume II deals principally with traffic accounts and the accounting of earnings and receipts
options.B: Volume I deals with traffic accounts, while Volume II deals with stores accounts
options.C: Volume I deals with workshop accounts, while Volume II deals with establishment accounts
options.D: Volume I deals with stores accounts, while Volume II deals with the general principles of railway accounting

e: Indian Railway Accounts Code Volume I covers general principles, books and compilation of accounts other than traffic accounts, while Volume II deals principally with traffic accounts and earnings.

q: A work is executed after considerable delay and, by the time it is completed, subsequent developments have made it serve no useful purpose. In audit terminology, the expenditure on such a work is termed:

options.A: Unsanctioned expenditure
options.B: Irregular expenditure
options.C: Infructuous expenditure
options.D: Provisional expenditure

e: Expenditure on a work that, by completion, serves no useful purpose due to delay and subsequent developments is termed infructuous expenditure in audit.

q: In 'audit against rules and orders', the scrutiny of the audit office is directed to seeing that:

options.A: The lowest tender has been accepted in every case
options.B: The accounts of the unit are arithmetically correct
options.C: The staff sanctioned for the office is adequate for its work
options.D: The orders issued by the executive authorities are not inconsistent with the governing rules and are within the competence of the authority issuing them

e: In audit against rules and orders, audit sees that executive orders are not inconsistent with governing rules and are within the competence of the issuing authority.

q: Under Article 322 of the Constitution, the expenses of which of the following, including the salaries, allowances and pensions payable to or in respect of its Chairman and members, are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India?

options.A: The Finance Commission
options.B: The Union Public Service Commission
options.C: The National Human Rights Commission
options.D: The Central Information Commission

e: Article 322 provides that expenses of the Union Public Service Commission, including salaries, allowances and pensions of its Chairman and members, are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

q: In voting a Demand for Grant, the Lok Sabha can do any of the following EXCEPT:

options.A: Increase the amount specified in the demand
options.B: Assent to the demand
options.C: Refuse assent to the demand
options.D: Assent to the demand subject to a reduction of the amount specified therein

e: Under Article 113, Lok Sabha may assent to, refuse or reduce a Demand for Grant, but it cannot increase the amount specified in the demand.

q: In an office, one official is allowed to receive cash, record it in the accounts and also reconcile the balances entirely by himself. The arrangement offends against a sound system of internal check because:

options.A: Internal check must be exercised only at the close of the financial year
options.B: The cashier should also maintain the ledger accounts
options.C: All stages of a transaction should be completed by one experienced official
options.D: No single person should be allowed to handle a transaction completely from the beginning to the end

e: A sound internal check requires division of work so that no single person handles a transaction completely from beginning to end, reducing scope for error and fraud.

q: The General Manager of a Railway does not accept the financial advice tendered by the Financial Adviser and Chief Accounts Officer in a matter. The proper course for the General Manager is to:

options.A: Overrule the advice without recording any reasons
options.B: Refer the matter to the Comptroller and Auditor General of India for a decision
options.C: Record his reasons in writing and report the matter to the Railway Board
options.D: Obtain fresh advice from the resident audit office

e: If the General Manager does not accept FA and CAO's financial advice, he must record his reasons in writing and report the matter to the Railway Board.

q: The first holder of the office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of independent India was:

options.A: A. K. Chanda
options.B: V. Narahari Rao
options.C: S. Ranganathan
options.D: T. N. Chaturvedi

e: V. Narahari Rao was the first Comptroller and Auditor General of independent India, succeeding the Auditor General under the Constitution.

q: The responsibility of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India for compiling the accounts of the Union and of each State, where that responsibility rests on him, is dealt with in the Comptroller and Auditor General's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971 under:

options.A: Section 10
options.B: Section 13
options.C: Section 16
options.D: Section 20

e: Section 10 of the CAG's DPC Act, 1971 deals with the CAG's responsibility for compiling accounts of the Union and of each State where that responsibility rests on him.

q: The Regulations on Audit and Accounts, laying down the principles, procedures and standards governing audit by the organisation of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, are framed under:

options.A: Article 150 of the Constitution
options.B: The General Financial Rules, 2017
options.C: Section 13 of the Comptroller and Auditor General's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971
options.D: Section 23 of the Comptroller and Auditor General's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971

e: Regulations on Audit and Accounts are framed by the CAG under Section 23 of the CAG's DPC Act, 1971, laying down principles, procedures and standards of audit.

q: A Vote on Account, by which the Lok Sabha makes grants in advance for a part of the financial year pending completion of the regular budget procedure, is normally taken for a period of:

options.A: One month
options.B: Four months
options.C: Two months
options.D: Six months

e: A Vote on Account is a grant in advance for part of the year pending completion of budget procedure under Article 116, normally taken for two months.

q: The earnings of Indian Railways, which form part of the receipts of the Union Government, are classified in the Union Budget as:

options.A: Tax revenue receipts
options.B: Non-tax revenue receipts
options.C: Capital receipts
options.D: Receipts under the Public Account of India

e: Railway earnings forming part of Union receipts are non-tax revenue receipts, since they are earnings from a departmental commercial undertaking, not taxes.

q: Long after the Public Accounts Committee had come into existence, Parliament constituted a second financial committee charged with examining the estimates and suggesting economies and improvements in organisation and efficiency. The Estimates Committee was first constituted in the year:
e: The Estimates Committee, Parliament's second financial committee after the Public Accounts Committee, was first constituted in 1950 to examine estimates and suggest economies.

q: The institution which, under the Constitution, became the office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India had its origin in the office of the Auditor General of India. That office was first created in the year:
e: The office of Auditor General of India, predecessor of the CAG under the Constitution, was first created in 1860.

q: The Special Railway Safety Fund, set up in the Budget for 2001-02 for clearing the backlog of safety-related renewal works, had a corpus of:

options.A: Rs 10,000 crore
options.B: Rs 25,000 crore
options.C: Rs 17,000 crore
options.D: Rs 1 lakh crore

e: The Special Railway Safety Fund set up in the Budget for 2001-02 for clearing backlog of safety-related renewals had a corpus of Rs 17,000 crore.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Railway Safety Fund from the Special Railway Safety Fund and the Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh?

options.A: The Railway Safety Fund finances the renewal of over-aged track and signalling assets
options.B: The Railway Safety Fund is utilised primarily for safety works at level crossings, such as manning of unmanned level crossings and construction of road over-bridges and road under-bridges
options.C: The Railway Safety Fund finances the construction of new lines in backward areas
options.D: The Railway Safety Fund meets the payment of compensation in railway accidents

e: The Railway Safety Fund is used primarily for safety works at level crossings, such as manning of unmanned crossings and construction of road over-bridges and road under-bridges.

q: The examination of the reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India relating to public undertakings, and of whether the affairs of those undertakings are being managed in accordance with sound business principles and prudent commercial practices, is a principal function of:

options.A: The Committee on Public Undertakings
options.B: The Estimates Committee
options.C: The Railway Convention Committee
options.D: The Departmentally Related Standing Committee on Railways

e: Examination of CAG reports on public undertakings and whether their affairs follow sound business principles and prudent commercial practices is a principal function of the Committee on Public Undertakings.

q: To watch the clearance of the objections raised by Audit in the Inspection Reports issued for its unit, the audited office maintains a register in which the objections and their settlement are recorded. The register is known as the:

options.A: Works Register
options.B: Liability Register
options.C: Suspense Register
options.D: Objection Book (Register)

e: The audited office records audit objections from Inspection Reports and their settlement in the Objection Book or Register, to watch their clearance.

q: Before a performance audit report is finalised, the audit office holds a conference with the audited entity to discuss the draft audit findings and observations and to obtain its response. This conference is known as:

options.A: An entry conference
options.B: A settlement conference
options.C: An exit conference
options.D: A vetting conference

e: Before a performance audit report is finalised, the exit conference is held with the audited entity to discuss draft findings and obtain its response.

q: In the commercial audit of Government companies, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is assisted by a body composed of officers of the Indian Audit and Accounts Department together with outside experts in the relevant fields. That body is known as the:

options.A: Audit Committee
options.B: Audit Board
options.C: Commercial Audit Wing
options.D: Company Law Board

e: In commercial audit of Government companies, the CAG is assisted by the Audit Board, comprising IA and AD officers together with outside experts in relevant fields.

q: A proposal suggests that the Contingency Fund of India can be created by an executive notification of the Ministry of Finance. The correct constitutional position is that the Fund is established:

options.A: By Parliament, by law, under Article 267 of the Constitution
options.B: By the President, by an ordinance, under Article 123
options.C: By a resolution of the Lok Sabha alone
options.D: By the Comptroller and Auditor General of India under Article 149

e: The Contingency Fund of India is established by Parliament by law under Article 267, and cannot be created merely by an executive notification.

q: During consideration of an Appropriation Bill, a member proposes an amendment that would alter the destination of a grant already voted by the Lok Sabha. Under Article 114 of the Constitution, such an amendment:

options.A: Can be moved in the Rajya Sabha only
options.B: Shall not be proposed in either House, since no amendment may vary the amount or alter the destination of any grant, or vary the amount of any charged expenditure
options.C: Can be moved with the concurrence of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: Can be moved if the Finance Minister agrees to it

e: Article 114(2) bars any amendment to an Appropriation Bill that varies the amount or alters the destination of a grant, or varies charged expenditure.

q: In the course of a financial year, additional expenditure beyond the grants already made becomes necessary, and expenditure already incurred in excess of a grant also awaits regularisation. Supplementary, additional or excess grants for such purposes are provided for in the Constitution under:

options.A: Article 112
options.B: Article 118
options.C: Article 115
options.D: Article 266

e: Supplementary, additional and excess grants, including regularisation of expenditure already incurred in excess of a grant, are provided for in Article 115.

q: Pending completion of the full budget procedure, the Lok Sabha is asked to make a grant in advance, and on another occasion to vote a large sum for an indefinite emergency demand. The power of the Lok Sabha to make a vote on account, a vote of credit and an exceptional grant is conferred by:

options.A: Article 110
options.B: Article 113
options.C: Article 280
options.D: Article 116

e: Article 116 empowers Lok Sabha to make grants in advance by vote on account, vote of credit for an indefinite emergency demand, and exceptional grants.

q: After his appointment, an attempt is made to revise the conditions of service of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India in a manner less favourable to him. The Constitution protects his independence by providing that his conditions of service:

options.A: Shall not be varied to his disadvantage after his appointment
options.B: Are fixed by the Public Accounts Committee
options.C: Are revised by the Finance Commission every five years
options.D: Are the same as those of a Cabinet Secretary

e: The proviso to Article 148(3) protects the CAG by providing that his conditions of service shall not be varied to his disadvantage after his appointment.

q: The audit of all expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India, to see that the moneys disbursed were legally available for the purpose applied, is a duty of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India dealt with in the Comptroller and Auditor General's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971 under:

options.A: Section 10
options.B: Section 13
options.C: Section 23
options.D: Section 16

e: Section 13 of the CAG's DPC Act, 1971 makes it the CAG's duty to audit all expenditure from the Consolidated Fund and see moneys were legally available for the purpose applied.

q: The President entrusts to the Comptroller and Auditor General of India the audit of the accounts of a body which is not otherwise subject to audit by him. Such entrusted audit, of accounts of certain authorities or bodies not otherwise covered, is dealt with in the Comptroller and Auditor General's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971 under:

options.A: Section 16
options.B: Section 17
options.C: Section 20
options.D: Section 13

e: Section 20 of the CAG's DPC Act, 1971 deals with audit entrusted to the CAG by the President or Governor of accounts of bodies not otherwise subject to his audit.

q: A newly appointed Comptroller and Auditor General of India is about to assume charge of his office. Before he can enter upon that office, he must make and subscribe the prescribed oath or affirmation before:

options.A: The Chief Justice of India
options.B: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
options.C: The Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee
options.D: The President of India, or some person appointed in that behalf by him

e: Article 148(2) requires the CAG, before entering office, to make and subscribe the prescribed oath or affirmation before the President or a person appointed by him.

q: Since 1967, a settled convention has governed the choice of the Chairperson of the Public Accounts Committee. Under that convention, the Chairperson is appointed from amongst the members belonging to:

options.A: The Opposition in the Lok Sabha
options.B: The ruling party in the Lok Sabha
options.C: The Rajya Sabha
options.D: The Estimates Committee

e: By convention since 1967, the Chairperson of the Public Accounts Committee is appointed from amongst members belonging to the Opposition in the Lok Sabha.

q: The Chairperson of the Estimates Committee of Parliament is appointed by:

options.A: The President of India
options.B: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha, from amongst the members of the Committee
options.C: The members of the Committee themselves
options.D: The Minister of Parliamentary Affairs

e: The Chairperson of the Estimates Committee is appointed by the Speaker of Lok Sabha from amongst the members of the Committee.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Comptroller and Auditor General of India audits all transactions of the Union relating to the Consolidated Fund of India.
2. His audit also extends to the transactions relating to the Contingency Fund of India and the Public Account of India.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Section 13 of the DPC Act, 1971 covers CAG audit of all transactions relating to the Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund and Public Account of India. Both statements are correct.

q: The internal audit organisation functioning on a zonal Railway, which reviews transactions after they have been processed by the executive and accounts offices, works under:

options.A: The Principal Director of Audit
options.B: The Financial Commissioner (Railways)
options.C: The Ministry of Finance
options.D: The Financial Adviser and Chief Accounts Officer of the Railway

e: Internal audit on a zonal Railway, reviewing transactions after processing by executive and accounts offices, functions under the FA and CAO of the Railway.

q: In the Balance Sheet forming part of the commercial accounts of Indian Railways, the capital-at-charge of the undertaking is shown:

options.A: On the liabilities side
options.B: On the assets side, along with the stores in stock
options.C: Only in the Finance Accounts of the Union
options.D: Under the Public Account of India

e: In the Railway Balance Sheet, capital-at-charge is shown on the liabilities side, representing Government investment in the undertaking against its assets.

q: After the merger of the Railway Budget with the General Budget, the surplus of Railways remaining after meeting its working expenses is:

options.A: Paid to General Finances as dividend, as before the merger
options.B: Retained by Railways and appropriated to its funds, such as the Depreciation Reserve Fund, Development Fund, Capital Fund and Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh
options.C: Credited to the Contingency Fund of India
options.D: Distributed among the State Governments

e: After merger, Railway surplus after working expenses is retained by Railways and appropriated to its funds like DRF, Development Fund, Capital Fund and RRSK, not paid as dividend.

q: The rules and procedure governing the compilation, consolidation and presentation of the accounts of Indian Railways are contained in:

options.A: The General Financial Rules, 2017
options.B: The Railways Act, 1989
options.C: The Indian Railway Accounts Code
options.D: The Delegation of Financial Powers Rules

e: Compilation, consolidation and presentation of Railway accounts are governed by the Indian Railway Accounts Code, the prescribed code for Railway accounting procedure.
